strengths: Significance: The expensive-target/cheap-helper formulation is useful. Hessian similarity permits substantial gradient bias and different minimizers, offering a meaningful alternative to requiring closely aligned tasks.

Originality and presentation: Equation (1) clearly explains the correction as approximating f−h. Extending this control-variate perspective to momentum, variance reduction, and decentralized helpers provides a useful unifying viewpoint.

Empirical evidence: The quadratic experiments separately vary gradient bias and curvature mismatch. The rotated-image and corrupted-label MNIST experiments illustrate AuxMom’s robustness relative to naive auxiliary updates.
Reproducibility: Appendix A supplies a code link, the neural-network architecture and several hyperparameters are specified, and extensive derivations enable scrutiny of the theoretical claims.

Limitations and ethics: The manuscript acknowledges fine-tuning’s reusable pretraining advantage, the restriction on obtaining MVR improvements with noisy helpers, and the additional weak-convexity assumption for multiple helpers. These are constructive disclosures. No material research-ethics concerns are apparent.
weaknesses: Soundness—AuxMom’s noise dependence is incorrect as stated. On page 20, the proof rewrites 128δηK(σ_f²+σ_h²)+(L/2+8δ)ησ_h² as 128LβKησ_f², but the defined β incorrectly assigns part of the helper-noise contribution to σ_f². Consequently, Theorem 3.2 contains σ_f²/K where the derivation requires a contribution proportional to σ_h²/K. Hessian similarity does not constrain these variances: even identical mean functions can have very different oracle noise. Without an additional variance restriction, the claimed bound can substantially underestimate the error.

Soundness—AuxMVR’s noisy-helper argument also has an unsupported transition. On page 25, choosing a=max(1/T,36δKη) leaves a target-noise term proportional to δKησ_f² in 3a(σ_f²+σ_h²). The subsequent bound instead uses 3888δ²K²η²σ_f². No assumed relationship between the two oracle variances justifies this replacement. Thus the stated general noisy-helper rate in Theorem 3.3 is not established.

The theorem specifications need reconciliation with their proofs. Theorem 3.2 uses K inside the stochastic stepsize denominator, whereas the balancing argument on page 20 uses K². The AuxMVR proof additionally requires an initial batch T times larger to control E0, but Theorem 3.3 does not state this requirement. These affect how the guarantees can be implemented and verified.

Evaluation and significance: Experiments cover only a scalar quadratic and one small MNIST network, and AuxMVR is not evaluated. Rotating images or changing labels does not demonstrate cheaper helper-gradient computation. Iteration plots, including the K comparison, therefore do not establish computational savings under matched total cost. Comparisons with closely related corrected-gradient methods and measurements of helper cost would strengthen the practical contribution.

Originality and scope: The paper explicitly identifies close connections to SVRG, MiMeSGDm, and MiMeMVR, but does not sharply isolate the new guarantees relative to these methods under comparable assumptions and oracle budgets. The broad application formulations are promising; their usefulness remains conditional on obtaining sufficiently similar, inexpensive helpers, which the experiments do not quantify.

Presentation and reproducibility: The manuscript omits experimental batch sizes, seed counts, uncertainty estimates, and sufficient baseline-tuning details. Inconsistent K versus K+1 update descriptions and the copied angle-based caption for Figure 6 further reduce precision. The code link is helpful, but the theoretical errors above are decisive: the central convergence claims require correction before acceptance.
